_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 5 Changing Materials. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. The five chapters are the five parts of LESSON["lecture"] in content/lesson-5.py, in its order and its words: same material back (ice melting and freezing, chocolate melting in the sun and setting in the fridge, both the demo's own frames); a new material (the egg of the experiment, predicted first, heated three times and cooled, drawn by the lesson's own ART.sim newMaterial); burning (wood to ash and smoke, and the candle that gets shorter); baking (dough into bread, cake mix into a cake); and the five heat rules of the Safe with heat step, including its misconception, that a pan which has stopped steaming is still hot. Every chapter ends on the lesson's one question: can you get the first material back?
title: Changing Materials
subtitle: Grade 2 Science
objectives: Know that some changes can turn a material into a different material.
Make predictions about what they think will happen.
Describe what happened during an enquiry and if it matched their predictions.
Follow instructions safely when doing practical work.

beats.say: Some changes make a new material. Some changes do not.
Ask one question: can you get the first material back?
Ice is a solid. Heat it and it melts into water, a liquid.
Put the water in the freezer, and it is ice again.
Melting and freezing keep the same material. It is water all along.
Chocolate melts in the sun. In the fridge it sets hard again.
It looks different, but it is still chocolate. You can get it back.
Here is a raw egg in a pan. The egg white is runny and clear.

at.egg: a raw egg in a pan

beats.say: Predict first. When the cooked egg cools, will it go back to raw?
Now heat it, three times. The clear part turns white and goes solid.
Now cool it down, and look. It stays cooked.
Say what happened, and whether it matched your prediction.
Cooking made a new material. You cannot get the egg back.
Wood burns in a fire. What is left is ash and smoke.
Can you turn the ash back into wood? No, you cannot.
A candle burns, too. It gets shorter as the wax burns away.
The wax turns into new materials that go off into the air.
Burning always makes a new material. It cannot come back.
Soft dough goes into the oven, and bread comes out.
Bread is a new material. There is no going back to dough.
Cake mix does the same. Runny mix goes in, and a cake comes out.
A baked cake cannot go back to being runny mix.
Heat can hurt. A grown-up handles the heating, and you watch.
Leave hot things for a grown-up to move, with oven gloves.
Never touch a pan to test if it is hot. Ask, or wait.

at.test: to test if it is hot

beats.say: Tie back long hair, and roll up your sleeves.
The steam stops, but the metal stays hot. Wait for it to cool.
Heat changes materials, and heat rules keep hands safe.
So now you know. Melting and freezing keep the same material.
Cooking, burning and baking make a new material. No going back.
Predict first, then test it and say what happened.
Keep safe with heat. And ask: can you get the first material back?
